docs.title: Run a heavy test once. Reuse the result safely everywhere
docs.text:
Aval signs a passing test result and ties it to the exact inputs it used. When another job has the same inputs and trusts the signer, it skips the test.

  1. List the inputs. Write the files and tools your test reads in aval.yaml. Aval hashes them into one fingerprint.
  2. Run once, sign the result. On a miss the test runs. Aval signs the result and pushes it to your own OCI registry.
  3. Verify, then skip. Same fingerprint and a trusted signer? The run is skipped. Anything unclear, the test runs.

If Aval cannot prove reuse is safe, the test runs. A bad signature fails with exit 5, never a silent miss.

docs.title: Artifact format
docs.text:
This document describes how Aval stores an execution result in an OCI registry, the attestation it signs, and the JSON that aval verify --output json prints. It is the contract external tools consume through pkg/evidence.

Status: pre-alpha. The Go types in pkg/evidence are the source of truth. Signing, push, lookup, fetch, verification and the policy file are implemented (attest.Sign, registry.Push, registry.Lookup, registry.Fetch, evidence.Verify, policy.Load). aval verify, aval run and aval push use them.

The identifiers below and the JSON shape of the statement, predicate and verify report are frozen. Within a version they change additively only; see Versioning and compatibility.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
All constants live in pkg/evidence.

Constant Value Used for Status ArtifactType application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 artifactType of the OCI manifest frozen ArtifactTypeFingerprint application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1 artifactType of the per-fingerprint anchor manifest frozen MediaTypeDSSE application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json Media type of the signed DSSE envelope layer DSSE standard MediaTypeExecution application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2+json Media type of the raw predicate JSON, when carried on its own frozen PayloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json DSSE payloadType in-toto standard StatementType https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1 in-toto Statement _type in-toto standard PredicateType https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2 in-toto predicateType frozen SchemaVersion v2 Predicate schemaVersion frozen ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 version of the verify report frozen RunRecordVersion aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1 version of a run record provisional ArtifactTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 artifactType of a run record manifest provisional MediaTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json Media type of the run record layer provisional ArtifactTypeStats application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1 artifactType of the per-test stats anchor manifest provisional

Registry identifiers (internal/registry): the bundle layer uses the Sigstore media type application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json (MediaTypeSigstoreBundle), and manifests carry the annotation io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint (AnnotationFingerprint, informational: verification reads the fingerprint from the signed predicate). The annotation key is frozen. The stats anchor carries io.trianalab.aval.test (AnnotationTest, provisional) with the test id.

Related identifiers from other packages: the fingerprint manifest format is aval-fingerprint/v1 (internal/fingerprint), and the contract and policy apiVersion is aval.trianalab.io/v1 (internal/contract, see contract.md). Both are frozen. The fingerprint manifest version is a format tag, not a namespaced identifier: it names the canonical manifest layout and hash, not a resource, so it stays outside aval.trianalab.io and is frozen as aval-fingerprint/v1; a breaking change mints aval-fingerprint/v2.

docs.title: OCI layout
docs.text:
There is no Aval server or database. The registry is the only index.

Per fingerprint there is one anchor manifest, and one execution manifest per execution whose subject is the anchor, so the OCI 1.1 referrers API lists every execution for a fingerprint.

The anchor is deterministic: its bytes, and so its digest, depend only on the fingerprint. It is tagged sha256-<fingerprint hex> (registry.Tag):

{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
      "size": 2,
      "data": "e30="
    }
  ],
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}

One execution = one OCI 1.1 image manifest, following the OCI 1.1 artifact guidance (artifactType set, empty config):

{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<envelope digest>",
      "size": 1834
    },
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<bundle digest>",
      "size": 4210
    }
  ],
  "subject": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:<anchor digest>",
    "size": 512
  },
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}
  • config: the OCI empty descriptor ({}, media type application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json).
  • layers: the signed DSSE envelope (see below), then the Sigstore bundle with the verification material. registry.Push refuses an attestation whose bundle is missing or is not valid JSON. If registry.Fetch reads a manifest without a bundle layer, the attestation can never verify, so it ends as a verification failure. registry.Fetch rejects any other layer, a repeated layer, or a missing envelope as a verification failure, and so a manifest that is not sha256-addressed, is larger than 4 MiB, or does not match the digest it was fetched by.
  • subject: always the anchor of the execution's fingerprint. The tested revision or artifact is recorded inside the statement (subject), not in the manifest, so the referrers of a tested image do not list its evidence.

The execution.v2 identifiers replace execution.v1, whose manifest had the tested artifact as an optional subject and exactly one layer. Aval no longer reads or writes v1: there is no accept window, and a v1 artifact is never a candidate.

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
registry.Push uploads the blobs, pushes the anchor and (re)tags it, then pushes the execution manifest by digest. It never moves or replaces an earlier execution: pushing the same bytes again is a no-op, and anything else becomes one more referrer of the anchor. Re-tagging the deterministic anchor also repairs a tag that was moved.

Registries without the referrers API (for example GHCR) are supported: oras maintains the OCI referrers tag schema (sha256-<anchor hex> index) on push and reads it on lookup. That index is rewritten on every push, so two concurrent pushes for the same fingerprint can drop one entry from it. Push therefore lists the anchor's referrers after pushing and returns only once the new digest is among them; if it is not, it pushes the manifest again (which re-adds it to the index) and lists again, three attempts in total, one second apart. If the digest is still not listed, aval push and aval run --push fail (exit 1). A registry that indexes referrers asynchronously for longer than about two seconds also fails the push; rerun it. Once a fingerprint has more than 64 attestations the confirmation listing fails too, so push exits 1. A dropped execution is never a candidate, so even then it never makes an unsigned or untrusted result reusable. Aval does not delete the previous referrers index after rewriting it, so pushing does not need DELETE rights.

docs.title: Lookup and consumption
docs.text:
1. Compute the fingerprint locally (aval run --fingerprint-only), e.g. sha256:3f9a....
  2. Resolve the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> in the repository passed via --registry. It must point at the anchor digest Aval computes locally for that fingerprint; anything else is a verification failure (the tag was moved).
  3. List the anchor's referrers with artifactType application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2. Each one is a candidate, identified by its manifest digest, even when the referrer entry is malformed (not an image manifest, not sha256): Fetch then rejects it as a verification failure, so it never turns into a miss.
  4. Fetch each candidate by digest (repo@sha256:...). Never fetch by tag: tags are mutable, digests aren't.
  5. Verify each envelope and apply the trust policy (see below).

Lookup accepts at most 64 candidates per fingerprint and makes at most 64 requests to list referrers, whatever paths the registry's Link headers point at. Above either limit it fails with outcome error (run the test), so whoever can push, or a buggy registry, cannot make aval verify fetch an unbounded number of manifests or pages.

A listed candidate whose manifest the registry answers with 404 (deleted, for example by an "untagged manifests" retention policy) is absent: it is skipped with a warning on stderr and is not part of rejected. If every candidate is absent, the outcome is a miss. Absence never hides a verification failure of another candidate.

Every registry call of one command runs under --registry-timeout (default 1m): lookup and every fetch share one deadline, and push has its own. A registry that stalls past it is outcome error (exit 1), so aval run runs the test; runner.command is never under this deadline. One credential store and one auth token cache are shared by all registry calls of a process.

A missing tag, or an anchor without executions, is a miss (evidence.ErrNotFound, exit code 4). An artifact that exists but is malformed or fails signature or policy checks is a verification failure (evidence.ErrVerification, exit code 5) and is a security event.

docs.title: Registry credentials
docs.text:
Aval reads registry credentials the way Docker does: from $DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json, or ~/.docker/config.json when DOCKER_CONFIG is not set, including the credential helpers it names (credsStore, credHelpers, for example docker-credential-osxkeychain or docker-credential-ecr-login). Log in with docker login <registry> (or oras login, which writes the same file). Without an entry for the registry, Aval connects anonymously, which is enough to read a public repository. Every registry call runs under --registry-timeout (default 1m; see Lookup and consumption).

A config file that cannot be parsed, or a helper that fails, is outcome error (exit 1): aval run runs the test and nothing is reused. Loopback registries (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) use plain HTTP; every other registry uses HTTPS.

docs.title: Multiple attestations per fingerprint
docs.text: Several executions can produce the same fingerprint (a developer run and a CI run, or a re-run). All of them stay listed as referrers of the anchor, so a later push cannot hide or replace an earlier one. aval verify verifies every candidate: the verified one with the highest trust level wins (ties go to a non-passed result, then the lowest digest). Candidates that are not used are listed in the report's rejected field; when any of them failed verification, stderr gets one aval: SECURITY: ... line. A candidate that cannot be fetched or checked (outcome error) might have outranked the verified one, so it blocks reuse and the test runs. A candidate that passes every check but whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel is rejected as miss: it was fully evaluated, so it does not block a verified sibling. When nothing is reused, the outcome is verification-failed when any candidate failed verification, otherwise error when any could not be checked, otherwise miss.

docs.title: The 64-candidate cap and cleanup
docs.text:
Every push adds one execution, even for the same inputs: the hostname and timestamps in the predicate differ. Aval never deletes one. Once a fingerprint has more than 64 executions, every lookup for it is outcome error: the test always runs. Every push for it still adds an execution, then fails its confirmation and exits 1. It stays that way until someone deletes executions. Other fingerprints are not affected, so the next change to an input also ends it.

To stay below the cap, push from one place (for example CI on the main branch). aval run --push does not push after it reuses a result, but aval run --shadow --push runs and pushes every time.

To clean up a fingerprint, list its executions and delete the ones you no longer need, for example with ORAS:

aval run --fingerprint-only            # prints sha256:<hex>
oras discover --artifact-type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 <repo>:sha256-<hex>
oras manifest delete <repo>@sha256:<execution digest>

The registry must allow deletes (registry:2 needs REGISTRY_STORAGE_DELETE_ENABLED=true; on GHCR, delete the package versions). Deleting executions is safe: it can make a result stop being reusable, never make an untrusted one reusable. Keep the one you still want to reuse, and keep any execution that failed verification until you have looked into it.

docs.title: Run records
docs.text:
aval run --record publishes one run record per run, for every outcome (verified, miss, error, verification-failed), so reuse can be measured from the registry alone. --record-file <path> writes the same record to a file, and aval record --record-file <path> publishes it later, for example from a CI job that has write credentials but runs no tests.

Records are statistics, never evidence. They are unsigned and informational. aval run and aval verify never fetch or read them, so a record, forged or not, cannot cause reuse, change an outcome or count toward the 64-candidate cap.

Recording is best-effort: a record that cannot be published (no write credentials, registry down, past --registry-timeout) or written prints aval: warning: run record not ... on stderr and never changes the exit code. Publishing has its own --registry-timeout deadline, so it cannot hold the command longer. --record needs --registry. Aval keeps no local state; a record file exists only when --record-file asks for one. An existing file at --record-file that is not an Aval result, report or valid run record is never overwritten: the run warns and goes on, and inside the contract scope that file stays an input of the fingerprint. A --record-file that is also --result or --report is not written either.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Per test there is one stats anchor, separate from every fingerprint anchor. It is deterministic (its digest depends on the test id alone) and tagged stats-<test id> (registry.StatsTag); fingerprint tags and OCI referrers tag schema tags start with sha256-, so the tags cannot collide. It has the same shape as the fingerprint anchor, with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1" and the annotation "io.trianalab.aval.test": "<test id>".

Each record is an OCI 1.1 image manifest with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1", the empty config, one layer of media type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json holding the record JSON, and the stats anchor as subject. Records are listed by the stats anchor's referrers. Unlike registry.Push, publishing a record does not confirm the referrers listing, so on a registry without the referrers API two concurrent records for one test can drop one of them. On such registries all records of a test also share one referrers index, which grows with every record; once it exceeds the registry's manifest size limit, publishing a record fails with a warning. Pruning old records is future work (Epic 9, #88).

docs.title: Record JSON
docs.text:
evidence.RunRecord, parsed by evidence.ParseRunRecord:

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always sha256:<hex>; empty when the fingerprint could not be computed. outcome string always The lookup decision, as in the verify report. reused bool always true when a verified result was reused and the test did not run. With --shadow, or when --report cannot be written, it is false. result string when known The reused or the real passed / failed; omitted when runner.command could not start. testDurationMs integer always How long runner.command ran, in milliseconds; 0 when it did not run. savedDurationMs integer always On reuse, the test duration recorded in the reused attestation (finishedAt - startedAt); 0 otherwise. avalVersion string always Version of the aval binary that ran. recordedAt RFC 3339 timestamp always When the record was made. ciRunUrl string when passed --ci-run-url, a link to the CI run. Aval does not derive it from any CI vendor.

Example:

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "reused": true,
  "result": "passed",
  "testDurationMs": 0,
  "savedDurationMs": 1184000,
  "avalVersion": "0.3.0",
  "recordedAt": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z",
  "ciRunUrl": "https://ci.example.com/acme/orders/runs/42"
}

docs.title: DSSE envelope
docs.text:
The layer is a DSSE envelope (evidence.Envelope):

{
  "payloadType": "application/vnd.in-toto+json",
  "payload": "<base64 of the in-toto Statement JSON>",
  "signatures": [
    { "keyid": "", "sig": "<base64 signature>" }
  ]
}

Signing uses sigstore-go (attest.Sign, keyless with a Fulcio certificate and Rekor entry, or key-based; see trust-model.md). It also produces a Sigstore bundle (application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json) carrying the certificate or key hint and the Rekor entry; it is stored as the second layer of the execution manifest. registry.Push requires it: aval verify checks the signature through the bundle (attest.Verifier), so an attestation without one could only ever be a verification failure.

docs.title: in-toto Statement
docs.text:
The envelope payload is an in-toto Statement v1 (evidence.Statement). Its subject is the tested revision or artifact, the same one recorded in predicate.subject.

{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1",
  "subject": [
    {
      "name": "git+https://github.com/acme/orders",
      "digest": { "gitCommit": "9b2c1e0f4a7d3b5c6e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d" }
    }
  ],
  "predicateType": "https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2",
  "predicate": { "...": "see below" }
}

For an image, use "digest": {"sha256": "<hex>"} with the image reference as name.

aval run records name = the test id and digest = {"sha256": "<fingerprint hex>"} (the declared inputs), runner.identity = the host name (a claim; trust comes from the signer), runner.trustLevel = 0, and execution.environment = os and arch plus the declared toolchain. Recording a git commit or image as the subject is milestone 3 work.

docs.title: Predicate
docs.text:
evidence.Predicate, JSON tags exactly as below. Required fields are the ones checked by Predicate.Validate (called by evidence.Parse).

Field Type Required Meaning schemaVersion string yes, must be v2 Predicate schema version. subject object yes Tested revision/artifact. subject.name string yes e.g. git+https://github.com/acme/orders or an image reference. subject.digest map string to string yes, non-empty e.g. {"gitCommit": "..."} or {"sha256": "..."}. test object Test identity: what was checked, independent of inputs. test.id string yes metadata.name from aval.yaml. test.cacheability string Class declared in the contract: hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic. result string yes passed or failed. execution object This run: its inputs and conditions. execution.fingerprint string yes, sha256:<64 hex> Fingerprint over the declared inputs. execution.fingerprintVersion string Manifest format, e.g. aval-fingerprint/v1. execution.environment map string to string no (omitted when empty) Conditions of the run (toolchain, OS/arch). Only keys declared under environment.toolchain in aval.yaml are part of the fingerprint; anything else here is informational. execution.exitCode integer Exit code of runner.command. runner object Who produced the result, as claimed. runner.identity string yes Claimed producer identity. runner.issuer string no (omitted when empty) Claimed identity issuer, e.g. an OIDC issuer URL. runner.trustLevel integer 0 unknown, 1 developer, 2 runner, 3 isolated. startedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes Execution start. finishedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes, not before startedAt Execution end. annotations map string to string no (omitted when empty) Free third-party metadata. Aval never reads it.

runner.identity, runner.issuer and runner.trustLevel are claims written by whoever produced the predicate. The authoritative identity and trust level are those of the verified signer, matched against the policy's accepted identities (evidence.Verification.Signer and its TrustLevel). Consumers must not make trust decisions from the runner block. The Go fields Runner.Issuer, Runner.TrustLevel and Verification.TrustLevel are deprecated: Aval leaves the first two empty, and the third duplicates Verification.Signer.TrustLevel.

evidence.Parse only checks structure. A parsed predicate is a claim, not evidence; use evidence.Verify to get something you can rely on.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: Keys use reverse-DNS of the owner, e.g. com.example.team, com.acme.ticket. Aval does not define, validate or interpret any key. Do not put secrets there: the predicate is published to the registry.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": "v2",
  "subject": {
    "name": "git+https://github.com/acme/orders",
    "digest": { "gitCommit": "9b2c1e0f4a7d3b5c6e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d" }
  },
  "test": {
    "id": "orders-integration",
    "cacheability": "controlled-environment"
  },
  "result": "passed",
  "execution": {
    "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
    "fingerprintVersion": "aval-fingerprint/v1",
    "environment": {
      "go": "1.23.4",
      "os": "linux",
      "arch": "amd64"
    },
    "exitCode": 0
  },
  "runner": {
    "identity": "https://github.com/acme/orders/.github/workflows/ci.yaml@refs/heads/main",
    "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "trustLevel": 2
  },
  "startedAt": "2026-11-05T10:12:03Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-11-05T10:31:47Z",
  "annotations": {
    "com.acme.team": "payments"
  }
}

docs.title: Verify report
docs.text:
aval verify --output json prints one evidence.Report to stdout, and aval run --report <file> writes the same document for its lookup decision. This is the stable machine interface for CI scripts and external tools.

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1. outcome string always See outcomes below. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always Locally computed sha256:<hex>. reference string when an attestation was found Immutable repo@sha256:<manifest digest>. result string verified only passed or failed from the verified predicate. signer object verified only Accepted policy identity that matched (issuer, subjectRegexp, trustLevel) plus the identity the signature actually carried: subject, the certificate subject (SAN) for keyless signatures, or keyId, base64(sha256(DER public key)) for key-based ones. subject and keyId are omitted when empty. predicate object verified only Full verified predicate. reason string non-verified outcomes Human-readable cause. rejected array when a candidate was not used Each {reference, outcome, reason}; outcome is verification-failed, error or miss. A verification-failed entry is a security event even when outcome is verified: alert. A miss entry is an authentic attestation whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel: routine non-reuse, no alert.

Outcomes and exit codes:

outcome Meaning What the caller does Exit code verified Valid attestation satisfies the policy. Reuse result. 0 miss No attestation for this fingerprint that the policy can reuse: none found, or only authentic ones whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel. Run the test. 4 verification-failed Attestation exists but fails signature or policy. Run the test and alert. Never hide this. 5 error Aval could not decide (registry unreachable, bad policy file, trusted root unavailable). Treat as a miss: run the test (fail closed). 1

These are the aval verify exit codes. aval run acts on the outcome and exits with the result instead; see trust-model.md.

If the fingerprint cannot be computed (empty scope, missing dependency, symlink, control characters in a path, I/O error), aval verify prints no report and exits 1; bad flags or an invalid contract print no report and exit 2. aval run --report still writes one in that case, with outcome error, the reason, and an empty fingerprint, and then runs the test.

Without --policy, aval verify skips the lookup and reports outcome: "miss" (exit 4), and so it does for a non-deterministic contract. With --policy, a policy file that cannot be loaded is outcome: "error" (exit 1) and no lookup is made. A trusted root that cannot be loaded is outcome: "error" (exit 1) once a candidate with a certificate needs it.

Example (verified):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reference": "ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval@sha256:8c1d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0",
  "result": "passed",
  "signer": {
    "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "subjectRegexp": "^https://github.com/acme/orders/\\.github/workflows/ci\\.yaml@refs/heads/main$",
    "trustLevel": 2,
    "subject": "https://github.com/acme/orders/.github/workflows/ci.yaml@refs/heads/main"
  },
  "predicate": { "...": "as in the predicate example" }
}

Example (miss):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "miss",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reason": "no attestation found for fingerprint"
}

docs.title: Versioning and compatibility
docs.text:
These rules apply to every frozen format:

Format Version identifiers (move together) Frozen at Statement and predicate PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution, ArtifactType .../execution/v2, v2, execution.v2 Fingerprint anchor ArtifactTypeFingerprint fingerprint.v1 Verify report, outcomes and exit codes ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 Run record and stats anchor RunRecordVersion, ArtifactTypeRun, MediaTypeRun, ArtifactTypeStats run-record/v1, run.v1, stats.v1 (provisional) Contract and policy file apiVersion aval.trianalab.io/v1 Fingerprint manifest header line, execution.fingerprintVersion aval-fingerprint/v1

The predicate keeps v2: v1 was used before and an identifier is never recycled, and v2 is already under aval.trianalab.io and is what v0.1.0 writes, so attestations published by v0.1.0 stay readable. The report and the contract moved from the pre-freeze aval.dev/.../v1alpha1 names to aval.trianalab.io at v1. There is no accept window for the old names: a contract or policy file with aval.dev/v1alpha1 is invalid.

docs.title: Additive changes (same identifier)
docs.text:
• A new optional field, omitted when empty, whose absence means what it meant before.
  • A new key under annotations.
  • A new optional contract field. Older aval binaries reject a contract that uses it (unknown fields are rejected), which fails closed.

Existing fields keep their name, JSON tag, type and meaning.

docs.title: Breaking changes (new identifier)
docs.text:
• Renaming or removing a field, changing its type or its meaning.
  • Making an optional field required, or tightening validation of an existing one.
  • A new value of a closed set: outcome, result, trustLevel, cacheability class, or an exit code.
  • A change to what the fingerprint covers or how it is hashed: a new aval-fingerprint/vN. There is no accept window: old attestations become misses, never false hits.

A new predicate version changes PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution and ArtifactType together (execution/v3, execution.v3). Old and new artifacts can coexist in one repository.

docs.title: How consumers treat versions
docs.text:
• Unknown version: not evidence. Reject a predicateType, schemaVersion, report version or artifactType you do not know, and run the test. evidence.Verify does this for predicates.
  • Unknown fields: ignore them within a version you know. Do not decode Aval documents strictly. evidence.Parse ignores unknown fields.
  • Unknown values of a closed set: fail closed. An outcome other than the four listed above, a result other than passed or failed, or an unknown trust level or cacheability class means "not verified": run the test. Within a version such a value can only come from a bug or tampering.
  • No field grants trust. Trust comes from the verified signer and the policy (see trust-model.md), never from a field that is new or that you do not understand.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text: Aval writes only the newest version of each format. When a breaking change mints a new version, the release notes say whether Aval keeps reading the old one for a transition. If it does, the old parser stays next to the new one, dispatching on the identifier, and old documents get no more trust than new ones; any identifier Aval does not know fails closed. Ending a transition is announced in the release notes of the release that removes it.

docs.title: Golden files
docs.text: pkg/evidence/testdata/statement-execution-v2.golden.json, pkg/evidence/testdata/verify-report-v1.golden.json and pkg/evidence/testdata/run-record-v1.golden.json set every field of the statement, predicate, verify report and run record. A test decodes each strictly into the current types and requires the same JSON back, so dropping, renaming or retyping a field, or adding a required one, fails. Another test requires every JSON field of those types to be set in its golden file, so a new field fails until it is added there. Golden files only grow: an existing field or value is never removed or changed, an additive change adds its new field to the golden file of its version, and a new version adds a new file next to the old ones.

docs.title: aval push
docs.text:
push signs the result recorded by 'aval run' and publishes it. The result must be for the current inputs: same test id, cacheability and fingerprint. Keyless signing reads the OIDC token from $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN.

Usage:
  aval push [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help                        help for push
      --key string                  signing key path (default: keyless OIDC)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (lookup and fetch share one; push has its own) (default 1m0s)
      --result string               result recorded by 'aval run' (default ".aval/result.json")

docs.title: aval record
docs.text:
record publishes a run record that 'aval run --record-file' wrote to the test's stats anchor in the registry, as 'aval run --record' would have. Use it to publish, from a job with write credentials that runs no tests, the record of a run made without them. Run records are unsigned statistics: run and verify never read them.

Usage:
  aval record [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help                        help for record
      --record-file string          run record written by 'aval run --record-file' (required)
      --registry string             OCI repository for run records (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (lookup and fetch share one; push has its own) (default 1m0s)

docs.title: aval run
docs.text:
run computes the execution fingerprint of the contract, looks for a signed attestation in the registry, and reuses it if it verifies against the trust policy. Otherwise it runs runner.command, records the result (--result) and, with --push, signs and publishes it.

Anything that cannot be proven runs the test: a fingerprint error, a registry or policy error, a miss. A verification failure also runs the test, and then exits 5: it is a security event. A reused failing result exits 3, like a failing run. --shadow verifies and still runs the test; if the verified result disagrees with the run, that is a false hit and run exits 1.

--record publishes a run record (outcome, reuse, durations) for statistics to the test's stats anchor in the registry, for every outcome. It is best-effort: a failure, such as missing write credentials, is a warning and never changes the exit code. Records are unsigned and never read by run or verify. --record-file writes the same record to a file for 'aval record'.

Exit codes: 0 passed or reused a pass, 3 failed or reused a failure, 5 verification failed (after running the test), 1 error or false hit, 2 usage. Keyless signing reads the OIDC token from $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN; runner.command never sees it.

Usage:
  aval run [flags]

Flags:
      --ci-run-url string           link to the CI run, stored in the run record
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
      --explain                     print the fingerprint manifest (what was hashed)
      --fingerprint-only            print the execution fingerprint and exit
  -h, --help                        help for run
      --key string                  signing key path for --push (default: keyless OIDC)
      --no-reuse                    always run, never reuse
      --policy string               trust policy file (required for reuse; without it the test always runs)
      --push                        sign and publish the result after running (needs --registry)
      --record                      publish a run record for statistics after the run (needs --registry; best-effort)
      --record-file string          also write the run record to this file, for 'aval record'
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (lookup and fetch share one; push has its own) (default 1m0s)
      --report string               also write the lookup decision as a verify report (JSON) to this file
      --result string               where to record the result for 'aval push' (default ".aval/result.json")
      --shadow                      verify, but run the test anyway and fail on a false hit

docs.title: aval verify
docs.text:
verify computes the fingerprint, looks up the attestation and verifies its signature and the trust policy, without running anything.

Exit codes: 0 verified, 4 miss, 5 verification failed (security event), 1 error (registry, policy or fingerprint), 2 usage or invalid aval.yaml.

Usage:
  aval verify [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help                        help for verify
  -o, --output string               output format: text or json (default "text")
      --policy string               trust policy file (without it every lookup is a miss)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (lookup and fetch share one; push has its own) (default 1m0s)

docs.title: The test contract: aval.yaml
docs.text:
Status: aval.trianalab.io/v1, frozen. Within v1 the schema changes additively only (see Versioning). Source of truth: internal/contract (schema, validation) and internal/fingerprint (what gets hashed). If this document and the code disagree, the code wins and this document has a bug.

The contract declares what a test is, how to run it, and which inputs it depends on. Aval reuses a previous result only when it can prove that the declared inputs are identical. Nothing is inferred: if an input is not declared, Aval cannot see it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1   # required, exact value
kind: Test                      # required, exact value

metadata:
  name: orders-integration      # test identity: WHAT is checked

runner:
  # argv, executed without a shell. Order matters and is part of the fingerprint.
  command: ["go", "test", "-tags=integration", "./orders/..."]

scope:
  source:                       # required, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "orders/**/*.go"
    - "internal/**/*.go"
    - "testdata/orders/**"
  exclude:                      # optional, removes files selected by source
    - "**/*_bench_test.go"
  dependencies:                 # optional, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "go.mod"
    - "go.sum"

environment:
  toolchain:                    # optional, declared, not detected (v0)
    go: "1.25"
  env:                          # optional, names only; values are hashed
    - CGO_ENABLED
    - GOFLAGS

cacheability: hermetic          # required, see "Cacheability classes"

Check it locally:

aval run -f path/to/aval.yaml --fingerprint-only   # prints sha256:<hex>
aval run -f path/to/aval.yaml --explain --fingerprint-only   # also prints the manifest

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
All fields below are the complete v1 schema. Unknown fields at any level are rejected (strict YAML decoding), so a typo such as sorce: fails instead of silently shrinking the scope. A file with more than one YAML document is rejected. Semantic validation reports all errors at once; YAML decoding errors (including unknown fields) are reported one at a time. An invalid contract exits with code 2 (usage).

Field Type Required Rules apiVersion string yes Must be aval.trianalab.io/v1. kind string yes Must be Test. metadata.name string yes 1-64 chars of [a-z0-9._-], starting and ending with [a-z0-9]. runner.command list of strings yes Non-empty argv. The first element must not be blank. No shell interpolation. v0 only supports this generic runner. scope.source list of globs yes At least one glob. Matched files are hashed. At fingerprint time, each glob must match at least one file (before exclude), and the set left after exclude must not be empty. scope.exclude list of globs no Removes files from the source set. Does not apply to dependencies. A glob may match nothing. scope.dependencies list of globs no Lockfiles and manifests. Each glob must match at least one file at fingerprint time. environment.toolchain map string to string no Keys match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$. Values are not validated. environment.env list of strings no Environment variable names matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. cacheability string yes One of hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic.

docs.title: Globs
docs.text:
All globs in scope.source, scope.exclude and scope.dependencies follow the same rules.

  • Slash-separated, relative to the directory that contains the contract file. That directory is the fingerprint root. Backslashes are rejected.
  • No leading /. No empty, . or .. segments (a//b, ./a, ../a are rejected), so a glob cannot escape the root. Likewise, a path with a leading / or such segments never matches any glob, not even **.
  • Each segment is matched with Go's path.Match (*, ?, [...]). * does not cross /. A malformed pattern (e.g. [a-) is rejected.
  • ** is only allowed as a whole segment and matches zero or more segments. src/**/*.go matches src/a.go and src/x/y/a.go. ** alone matches every file. foo** or **.go are rejected. Consecutive ** match the same names as one (**/**/x is **/x), and matching takes time proportional to glob segments times path segments, however many **.
  • In exclude, a trailing ** means the files under a directory: a file named build that only build/** would exclude fails fingerprinting (see "Fail-closed errors"). Exclude such a file by name (build).
  • Globs match files only, never directories. To include a directory's contents, write dir/**.
  • The order of globs does not matter.

docs.title: Test identity vs execution fingerprint
docs.text:
• Test identity is metadata.name: what is being checked, stable across executions (e.g. orders-integration).
  • Execution fingerprint is a SHA-256 over the concrete inputs and conditions of one execution: the contract itself, the content of every file in scope, the declared toolchain and the declared environment values. Two executions with the same fingerprint are, as far as the contract can tell, the same execution.

The name is also part of the fingerprint (through the contract hash), so renaming a test produces a new fingerprint.

docs.title: Cacheability classes
docs.text:
Class Meaning Reusable by default hermetic Result depends only on declared files and toolchain. yes controlled-environment Depends on services/images whose versions are pinned inside the scope (e.g. a compose file with image digests). yes external-dependencies Talks to things outside the scope (SaaS APIs, shared databases). no, only with explicit policy opt-in non-deterministic Results vary between runs with identical inputs. never

"Reusable by default" only means the class does not block reuse. A result is still reused only if a valid, signed attestation exists and the trust policy accepts its signer (see trust-model.md). Without a policy nothing is accepted. aval run prints cacheability external-dependencies: not reusable by default (the policy may allow it) and cacheability non-deterministic: never reusable. A non-deterministic test is never looked up: it always runs.

docs.title: What goes into the fingerprint
docs.text:
The fingerprint is sha256:<hex> of a canonical, line-oriented manifest (format aval-fingerprint/v1). aval run --explain prints the exact text that was hashed. Layout, in this order:

aval-fingerprint/v1
contract <sha256 of canonical contract JSON>
source <sha256> <mode> <path>
dependency <sha256> <mode> <path>
toolchain <key>=<value>
env <NAME> <sha256 of value | unset>
  • Header: aval-fingerprint/v1. Bumped whenever the layout changes, so fingerprints from different formats never collide.
  • contract: SHA-256 of the contract serialized as JSON after parsing. Comments, formatting and YAML key order do not matter. Set-like lists (source, exclude, dependencies, env) are sorted and deduplicated first, so their order does not matter. runner.command is not sorted: argv order is semantic. Map keys (toolchain) are sorted by the JSON encoder. Every field is included, so changing metadata.name, runner.command or cacheability changes the fingerprint. An explicitly empty list or map (exclude: []) hashes the same as an omitted field.
  • source: one line per file that matches any source glob and no exclude glob.
  • dependency: one line per file that matches any dependencies glob. A file matched by both source and dependencies appears in both sections.
  • File lines carry the SHA-256 of the file content, a portable mode (x if any execute bit is set, - otherwise) and the slash-separated path relative to the root. Owner, timestamps and other permission bits are not hashed.
  • toolchain: one line per declared entry, key=value, as written. v0 trusts the declaration; it does not check the installed toolchain.
  • env: one line per declared variable with the SHA-256 of its value, or unset if the variable is not set. Set-but-empty and unset are different. Values are never written in clear.

Lines are sorted within each section. The result does not depend on checkout path, directory iteration order or glob order. The x mode is taken from the filesystem, so Windows (which has no execute bit) and Unix checkouts of the same executable file fingerprint differently.

Paths are hashed as the bytes the filesystem returns, never normalized. The NFC and NFD spellings of the same visible name (café.go) are different inputs, and so are A.go and a.go. Globs match those bytes case-sensitively and without normalization. A literal glob that differs from the on-disk name only by case or Unicode form (Makefile vs makefile) matches nothing, so fingerprinting fails (see "Fail-closed errors"). A wildcard glob that matches other files (**/Makefile) still leaves such a file out of scope, like any undeclared file.

docs.title: What does not go in
docs.text:
• Files not matched by source or dependencies. Undeclared inputs are invisible: if the test reads them, Aval cannot detect a change. This is the main risk of declared scope; keep the scope honest.
  • .git directories at any depth (skipped entirely). The name match is exact and case-sensitive: a .GIT directory is not skipped. A regular file named .git (a worktree or submodule pointer) is an ordinary file: it is in scope if a glob matches it.
  • Aval's own outputs, so a broad scope such as ["**"] keeps its fingerprint across aval runs and aval push accepts the recorded result:
  • .aval directories at any depth (skipped entirely, the same exact, case-sensitive name match as .git). .aval/ is reserved for Aval: a file the test reads must not live there.
  • The --result and --report files the command is given, when they fall inside the contract root. Each command knows only its own flags: aval push skips its --result, aval verify neither. A custom path outside .aval/ is therefore hashed by a command that is not given it (a miss, never a false hit); keep results and reports under .aval/ or outside the root. A --result or --report path that the scope includes and that holds anything other than an Aval result or report (a real input) exits 2 before the test runs: skipping it would drop that input from the fingerprint. aval run also refuses, with exit 2, to overwrite any existing file at those paths that is not an Aval result or report, wherever it lies.
  • The git commit, branch or any VCS metadata. Two commits with identical scope content produce the same fingerprint and can reuse the same result. That is intended: a commit that only touches unrelated files should not force a re-run.
  • Environment variables not listed in environment.env.
  • The real toolchain version, OS and architecture, unless declared.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
Declared scope means some relevant changes are invisible by design (invariant 2 in AGENTS.md). A test that depends on one of these can reuse a result it should not. The first two are pinned by gap rows in the false-hit corpus (internal/fingerprint/corpus_test.go), which assert the fingerprint does not change; the others follow from what the manifest hashes (see above):

  • A file the test reads but scope does not match (corpus row), including a name that differs from a wildcard glob by case or Unicode form.
  • An environment variable the test reads but environment.env does not list (corpus row).
  • Content behind a declared name: a container tag such as postgres:16 that is repushed, a dependency fetched from the network at run time, a service reached over the network. Only the declared text is hashed. Pin digests inside the scope (controlled-environment) or use external-dependencies, which is not reusable by default.
  • The installed toolchain, OS and architecture: environment.toolchain is trusted as written (see "Future work").

Mitigations: contract review, the cacheability classes, aval run --shadow (runs the test anyway and fails on a false hit) and, in the future, observed inputs.

docs.title: False-hit corpus
docs.text:
TestFalseHitCorpus applies every known kind of change to one base project and asserts its outcome: a relevant change (content, rename, add, delete, exec bit, lockfile, toolchain, env value or presence, command, any contract field, re-included excludes) changes the fingerprint; an irrelevant one (out-of-scope or excluded files, .git, Aval's own outputs, checkout path, ordering, duplicates, timestamps, non-exec permission bits, YAML formatting) does not; an unprovable one (see "Fail-closed errors") fails closed. The test fails if a manifest section is changed by no differ row, so a new section must come with corpus cases; a new attribute in an existing section or a new contract field needs its row added by review.

TestManifestGolden pins, per manifest version, the manifests of three contracts over a fixed tree (internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden/tree), concatenated in testdata/golden/aval-fingerprint-vN.manifest. One contract sets every field: source, exclude, dependencies and env each unsorted and with a repeat, a toolchain map with six keys, argv with &, <, > and non-ASCII characters, and env vars that are set, set to the empty string and unset. One omits every optional field; one sets every optional field to an empty list or map and must encode like the one that omits them (TestGoldenOmittedEqualsEmpty). The tree has a nested path, a path with a space, a file that sorts differently by full path than in walk order (pkg.go before pkg/...), an empty file under a dot-directory, content with CRLF line endings, an excluded file and a file outside the scope. The test adds a top-level and a nested .git directory (skipped) and a regular file named .git (in scope), and fixes the env values and the file modes: one exec bit each for owner (0744), group (0654) and other (0645), all three (0755), and a file with setuid, setgid and sticky but no exec bit. Any change to how these manifests are built (their lines, the hashes in them or the canonical contract JSON) fails it unless the header version is bumped too, so an old fingerprint can never mean different inputs.

What this covers was measured by mutation: each conditional, constant, format string and normalization in Compute, canonicalContract, listFiles, hashMatching, hashFile, sum and the glob matcher was mutated and make ci-false-hit run; every mutant that changes the manifest of some input fails it, through the golden, the corpus, the glob tables or the fail-closed tests. The two mutants that pass are equivalent on the platforms CI runs: dropping filepath.ToSlash (the separator is already / on Unix) and masking with Mode().Perm()&0o111 instead of Mode()&0o111. A path the tree does not exercise (a new manifest feature) is caught only by the corpus, so it must come with a case in the golden tree.

TestGoldensAppendOnly stops the golden being rewritten to match: a committed *.manifest golden may be added (a new version) but never modified, renamed or deleted. It diffs the goldens against the merge base of HEAD and AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE; in CI that is the PR base branch or the commit before the push, and the test fails if it does not resolve (after a force-push to main the old commit may be unreachable, and the job fails until the next normal push). Locally make ci-false-hit sets it to origin/main when it is unset, and the test fails when that ref is missing, so set AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE to the upstream main if your remote is named differently. A plain go test without AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE (the ci-engine job and the dogfood suite, which check out shallow) skips this one test; the ci-false-hit leg never does. TestGoldenEditsCatchesEdits is its negative test; by hand, append a line to the golden and run AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE=HEAD go test ./internal/fingerprint -run TestGoldensAppendOnly. The ci-false-hit CI job (make ci-false-hit, part of make ci) runs these tests and the glob tables on every PR and push, with no path filter. TestFalseHitGateIsBinding (tests/architecture) fails if that job or leg is removed, made conditional, allowed to fail (continue-on-error), checked out shallow, or given any other AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE, or if the recipe of make ci-false-hit changes in any way (a -skip, a dropped package, a dropped -count=1, a dropped AVAL_GOLDEN_BASE default). Edits to the tests themselves are left to review.

docs.title: Fail-closed errors
docs.text:
If equivalence of inputs cannot be proven, fingerprinting fails and the test must run. aval run reports the reason (outcome error) and runs the test without recording it; aval run --fingerprint-only, --explain, aval verify and aval push exit with code 1. The cases:

  • source glob "<glob>" matched no files: every source glob must match at least one file before exclude is applied. A typo or a name that differs by case or Unicode form would otherwise silently drop a declared input.
  • scope.source matched no files (after applying exclude).
  • source "<path>" is excluded only by a trailing "**": an exclude glob such as build/** matches a file named build only because ** matches zero segments. Exclude the file by name or narrow the glob.
  • dependency glob "<glob>" matched no files: every dependencies glob must match at least one file.
  • A file in scope is not a regular file (symlink, device, socket, ...): only regular files are supported in scope. A symlink's target may live outside the scope, so it cannot be proven unchanged.
  • A path in scope contains a newline or carriage return: control characters in path are not supported. The manifest is line-oriented, so such a name could forge manifest lines and collide with a different tree.
  • Any I/O error while walking or reading the root. The walk only enters directories that a source or dependencies glob can match a file in, so an unreadable directory outside the scope (a root-owned volume, a cache) is never opened and causes no error. exclude does not prune the walk.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
aval run -f aval.yaml --fingerprint-only            # sha256:<hex>
aval run -f aval.yaml --explain --fingerprint-only  # manifest, then digest

To find out why two environments disagree, diff the --explain output from both. The differing line names the file, toolchain entry or variable.

-f defaults to aval.yaml in the current directory. The root is always the directory of the contract file, not the current directory.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
apiVersion aval.trianalab.io/v1 is frozen. Policy files (kind: Policy) use the same value. Within v1 the schema only gets new optional fields: existing contracts keep parsing and keep their meaning. Because unknown fields are rejected, an older aval rejects a contract that uses a field it does not know, which fails closed. Renaming or removing a field, changing its type or meaning, or tightening its validation needs a new apiVersion.

The pre-freeze aval.dev/v1alpha1 is not accepted: change the line to aval.trianalab.io/v1. The contract hash covers apiVersion, so results published under the old value become misses and the tests run once. The general rules are in artifact-format.md.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Detected toolchain: verify or record the installed toolchain instead of trusting environment.toolchain. Not scheduled in milestones 1-5.
  • Observed inputs: trace which files the test actually reads, to flag undeclared inputs or suggest scope. v0 never infers scope.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Aval is one static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64. The installers download it from GitHub Releases and check it before installing. This site serves the installers of the latest commit on main; the same files are scripts/get-aval.sh and scripts/install.ps1 in the repository.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash

The script needs curl or wget and sha256sum or shasum, and works with the bash 3.2 that macOS ships. It installs aval into /usr/local/bin and uses sudo only when that directory is not writable.

Variable or flag Effect DESIRED_VERSION=v0.2.0, --version v0.2.0 install this release instead of the latest AVAL_INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin install into this directory USE_SUDO=false, --no-sudo never use sudo AVAL_NO_VERIFY=1, --no-verify skip the signature and provenance checks (the sha256 is still checked) AVAL_DOWNLOAD_URL download from a mirror of the release files; the signer identity does not change

Flags need the script as a file, or bash -s -- when piped:

curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.2.0

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
In PowerShell 5.1 or 7:

irm https://aval.run/install.ps1 | iex

It installs aval.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval and adds that directory to the user PATH, without administrator rights. It reads DESIRED_VERSION, AVAL_INSTALL_DIR, AVAL_NO_VERIFY and AVAL_DOWNLOAD_URL from the environment.

docs.title: What the installers check
docs.text:
Both scripts stop without installing anything when a check fails:

  1. checksums.txt must exist in the release and list the archive, and the archive must have that sha256. This check always runs.
  2. If cosign is on PATH, checksums.txt must carry a keyless Sigstore signature from https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/<tag>.
  3. If gh 2.49 or later is on PATH, the archive must match the SLSA provenance from the same workflow (gh attestation verify with the provenance.sigstore.json bundle of the release; no GitHub login needed).

Without cosign or gh, the installer prints which check did not run. To check a downloaded release by hand:

cosign verify-blob checksums.txt --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/v0.2.0
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
gh attestation verify aval_0.2.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz --bundle provenance.sigstore.json --repo TrianaLab/aval

docs.title: Go users
docs.text: go install github.com/TrianaLab/aval/cmd/aval@latest builds from source instead. The binary reports version dev and skips the release checks above.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Delete the binary: /usr/local/bin/aval (or your AVAL_INSTALL_DIR), or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval on Windows, and remove that directory from the user PATH.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Status: pre-alpha. Milestone 1 (contract + fingerprint) is implemented. Milestone 2 (sign, push, verify, aval run reuse or execute) is implemented. The consumption contract is stable: the media types, the predicate type and the report version are frozen, and the compatibility rules are in artifact-format.md.

docs.title: Consuming Aval evidence
docs.text: Aval produces signed test execution results. Other tools (CI systems, release gates, dashboards, policy engines) may consume them. There are three surfaces meant for that. Anything else in the repository (internal/..., the text output of the CLI, the fingerprint manifest layout) is not a consumption contract.

docs.title: 1. OCI artifact and predicate format
docs.text:
An execution result is an in-toto v1 Statement wrapped in a DSSE envelope, stored in an OCI registry, found through the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> and the OCI 1.1 referrers of the manifest it points at, and consumed by digest. The predicate type is https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2.

See artifact-format.md for the media types, manifest layout and predicate fields.

Predicate fields are neutral on purpose: subject, test.id, test.cacheability, result, execution.fingerprint, execution.fingerprintVersion, execution.environment, execution.exitCode, runner, startedAt, finishedAt, and a free annotations map. Within v2 only additive changes are allowed.

docs.title: 2. Go package github.com/TrianaLab/aval/pkg/evidence
docs.text:
pkg/evidence has no dependency on the rest of the module and is the only public Go API. It exposes:

Symbol Purpose Parse(data []byte) (*Predicate, error) Decode predicate JSON and run Validate. Does not check signatures. (*Predicate).Validate() error Structural checks: schemaVersion == "v2", subject, test.id, result, fingerprint format sha256:<64 hex>, runner.identity, timestamps. Verify(ctx, *Envelope, VerifyOptions) (*Verification, error) Check the signature with VerifyOptions.Signature, match the signer against the accepted identities, enforce the minimum trust level, decode the statement and predicate, and require the expected fingerprint, test id and a reusable cacheability. Every failure is a *VerificationError. SignatureVerifier, Signer VerifySignature(ctx, *Envelope) (Signer, error) checks the signature cryptographically and returns the signer it binds (Issuer and Subject of a keyless certificate, or KeyID). It applies no policy. pkg/evidence ships no implementation, to stay free of Sigstore dependencies; Aval's own is internal/attest.Verifier over the Sigstore bundle. A public Sigstore implementation for consumers is planned for milestone 5. MatchIdentity(ids, issuer, subject) (Identity, bool) The accepted keyless identity that grants a signer the highest trust level. The issuer must be equal; SubjectRegexp must match the whole subject (anchored); an invalid regexp matches nothing. Entries with a PublicKey never match. The level comes from the policy, never from the predicate. MatchSigner(ids, Signer) (Identity, bool) MatchIdentity for keyless signers; for key-based ones, the entries whose PublicKey has the signer's KeyID. The returned identity carries the signer's real Subject / KeyID. PublicKeyID(pem) (string, error) base64(sha256(DER)) of a PEM public key: the key hint in key-based Sigstore bundles. VerifyOptions Expected fingerprint and test id (both required), accepted Identities (empty accepts nothing), MinTrustLevel (level 0 and levels above 3 are never accepted), AllowedCacheability (hermetic and controlled-environment always; external-dependencies only if listed; non-deterministic never), Signature (required). ErrNotFound No attestation exists for the fingerprint. A miss; re-run. ErrVerification An attestation exists but failed signature or policy checks. Security event. *VerificationError wraps it with a reason. Report, ReportVersion The document printed by aval verify --output json. RunRecord, RunRecordVersion, ParseRunRecord(data []byte) (*RunRecord, error) A run record published by aval run --record (see artifact-format.md). Unsigned statistics: never a basis for reuse or trust. ParseRunRecord checks the version, testId and the closed sets only.

Trust levels: 1 developer (personal acceleration, not full trust), 2 CI runner with verifiable identity, 3 isolated execution with verifiable attestation of the environment. 0 (unknown) is never accepted.

A complete external consumer lives in examples/evidence-consumer: its own Go module that imports only pkg/evidence and the standard library, brings its own SignatureVerifier (ed25519 over the DSSE encoding), keeps a miss apart from a verification failure, and reads aval verify reports. CI builds and tests it against the checked-out pkg/evidence (make example), and tests/architecture fails if it imports any other Aval package.

The shorter sketch below shows the same flow. How the envelope bytes are fetched (ORAS, a registry client, aval) is up to the consumer; fetch by digest, not by tag.

package consumer

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "errors"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/TrianaLab/aval/pkg/evidence"
)

// CheckResult returns the verified predicate for testID at fingerprint, or an
// error. envBytes is the DSSE envelope layer, fetched by digest; sig checks
// its signature, typically with sigstore-go over the bundle layer.
func CheckResult(ctx context.Context, envBytes []byte, sig evidence.SignatureVerifier, testID, fingerprint string) (*evidence.Predicate, error) {
    var env evidence.Envelope
    if err := json.Unmarshal(envBytes, &env); err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("decoding envelope: %w", err)
    }
    v, err := evidence.Verify(ctx, &env, evidence.VerifyOptions{
        ExpectedFingerprint: fingerprint,
        ExpectedTestID:      testID,
        Identities: []evidence.Identity{{
            Issuer:        "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
            SubjectRegexp: `^https://github\.com/acme/orders/\.github/workflows/ci\.yml@refs/heads/main$`,
            TrustLevel:    evidence.TrustRunner,
        }},
        MinTrustLevel: evidence.TrustRunner,
        Signature:     sig,
    })
    switch {
    case errors.Is(err, evidence.ErrVerification):
        // Someone published a result we do not trust. Alert, do not reuse.
        return nil, err
    case err != nil:
        // Not reachable from Verify today, but fail closed. Do not reuse.
        return nil, err
    }
    if v.Predicate.Result != evidence.ResultPassed {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("test %s failed at %s", testID, fingerprint)
    }
    return v.Predicate, nil
}

ErrNotFound is returned by the lookup step (the registry client), not by Verify: if there is no envelope to pass in, it is a miss.

docs.title: Go API compatibility
docs.text:
pkg/evidence follows semantic versioning as part of the module github.com/TrianaLab/aval. Within a major version its exported API changes additively only: new identifiers, new struct fields that keep a comparable struct comparable, new methods on concrete types. Removing or renaming an exported identifier, changing a type, a field type, a function or method signature or a receiver, making a struct non-comparable, or adding a method to an exported interface is a breaking change and needs a new major version, which in Go means a new module path (github.com/TrianaLab/aval/v2). The release that ships it is tagged v2.0.0 or later (Go rejects a /v2 module tagged v0 or v1), so its changeset sets the version explicitly rather than relying on a major bump from 0.x.

This is enforced, not only documented. The exported surface is snapshotted in pkg/evidence/testdata/api-v1.txt, named after the major version in go.mod: one line per exported constant, variable, function, type, field (embedded fields included, with its struct tag: a changed JSON name or omitempty is breaking) and method, with types, signatures, type parameters and constraints and without parameter names (type parameter names and the order of union terms are kept, so changing them needs a snapshot change too). Fields promoted through embedding get a promoted <Type>.<Field> line, so one that becomes ambiguous or changes type is breaking. Methods are the full method set, promoted ones included, with the receiver (T or *T) they need. Interfaces are one line with their whole method set or type set. A struct that supports == also gets a comparable <Type> line. A constant of a type the package declares (TrustLevel, Result, Outcome) is rendered with its value, since consumers compare those values: policy files write trust levels by name, but verify reports and predicates carry them as numbers (the mapping is in trust-model.md), so renumbering TrustRunner is breaking. Untyped constants (the format identifiers) are rendered without their value (see below).

make ci-gates (TestEvidenceAPIIsAppendOnly in tests/architecture) fails when:

  • a line of the snapshot no longer matches the code;
  • the code exports something the snapshot lacks (an additive change appends its lines in the same pull request);
  • the exported API names an unexported type of the package (an embedded, returned or field type), whose members would not be rendered;
  • a non-test file of pkg/evidence has any build constraint: a //go:build or // +build line (GOOS, GOARCH, cgo, a go1.N release tag or a custom tag), import "C", or a _GOOS/_GOARCH file name suffix. The snapshot is taken on one platform and toolchain, and consumers build the library on any, so every file must be built everywhere;
  • a line of the snapshot at the base revision is missing from the current snapshot, so a break cannot be hidden by editing both. The base is the merge base with origin/<base branch> on a pull request, the commit main pointed to before a push to main (before of the push event, so all the commits of one push are compared together), and the merge base with origin/main otherwise. In CI (CI set) an unresolvable base fails the job; locally, without origin/main, this one comparison is skipped with a log line.

A new major module path starts a new snapshot file, which has no base to compare with.

The Go API and the wire formats are versioned separately. The predicate type, media types, report version and apiVersion follow artifact-format.md: a breaking format change gets a new identifier. Supporting a new format version is an additive Go change (new constants or types next to the old ones); the values of the untyped constants are format identifiers, so changing them is governed by the format rules rather than by the API snapshot. Outcome values are both: they are in the snapshot and in the verify report format. Dropping a type or constant a consumer may still use is a breaking Go change and needs a new major module path, even when the format it described is retired.

docs.title: 3. aval verify --output json
docs.text:
aval verify computes the fingerprint from aval.yaml, looks up the attestation, verifies it against the trust policy and runs nothing. With --output json (-o json) it prints an evidence.Report on stdout. Once the report is printed its reason is the only copy of the error message; stderr adds one aval: SECURITY: ... line when an attestation failed verification. Errors before there is a report (flags, aval.yaml) go to stderr.

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "reference": "ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval@sha256:...",
  "result": "passed",
  "signer": { "issuer": "...", "subjectRegexp": "...", "trustLevel": 2 },
  "predicate": { "...": "..." }
}

reference, result, signer, predicate, reason and rejected are omitted when empty. reason is set for miss, verification-failed and error. rejected lists candidate attestations that were not used, each {reference, outcome, reason} with outcome verification-failed, error or miss. A verification-failed entry is a security event even when the report's outcome is verified. A miss entry is an authentic attestation from a signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel: routine non-reuse, not a security event.

Exit code outcome Meaning What to do 0 verified A valid attestation satisfies the policy. Reuse result. 4 miss No attestation for this fingerprint that the policy can reuse (none found, or only signers the policy lists below minTrustLevel). Run the test. 5 verification-failed Attestation exists but failed signature or policy. Run the test and alert. 1 error (may have no report if fingerprinting failed) Aval could not decide (registry down, I/O, bad policy file, trusted root unavailable). Run the test (fail closed). 2 (no report) Bad flags or invalid aval.yaml, checked before anything runs: a --registry that is not an OCI repository (ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval, no scheme, tag or digest), --push or aval push with a --key that does not load or with neither a key nor $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN, a --result or --report path that holds an input of the test or, for aval run, any existing file that is not an Aval result or report. Fix the invocation.

CI snippet that keeps miss and verification failure apart:

set +e
report=$(aval verify --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy aval-policy.yaml -o json)
code=$?
set -e

outcome=$(jq -r '.outcome // "error"' <<<"$report")
case "$code:$outcome" in
  0:verified)
    if jq -e '[.rejected[]? | select(.outcome == "verification-failed")] | length > 0' <<<"$report" >/dev/null; then
      ./notify-security.sh "$report" # a rejected candidate failed verification
    fi
    echo "reusing $(jq -r .reference <<<"$report") (result: $(jq -r .result <<<"$report"))"
    [ "$(jq -r .result <<<"$report")" = passed ] || exit 1
    ;;
  4:miss)
    echo "no attestation for $(jq -r .fingerprint <<<"$report"), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  5:verification-failed)
    echo "::error::untrusted attestation for $(jq -r .testId <<<"$report"): $(jq -r .reason <<<"$report")"
    ./notify-security.sh "$report"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  *)
    echo "aval could not decide (exit $code), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
esac

Check both the exit code and outcome; if they disagree, treat it as error. The policy file format (--policy) is described in trust-model.md.

docs.title: Guidance for consumers
docs.text:
• Always verify. Parse and Validate only check structure. A parsed predicate is a claim, not evidence. runner.identity inside the predicate is self-reported; the authoritative identity is the verified signer.
  • Treat verification-failed as a security event. Log it, alert on it, never fold it into "miss" or silently re-run without a trace.
  • Fail closed. Any outcome other than verified means run the test.
  • Consume by digest. Tags are only for lookup.
  • Pin versions. Check schemaVersion == "v2" on predicates (Validate does this) and version == "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1" on reports. Reject versions you do not know. Within a version, ignore unknown fields: changes are additive.
  • Respect cacheability. non-deterministic results are never reusable; do not widen that in your adapter.

docs.title: Example: Pacto as an external consumer
docs.text:
This is a conceptual example of an integration that lives outside Aval. Aval does not import or depend on Pacto and knows nothing about Pacto concepts.

Pacto could consume Aval results through pkg/evidence or aval verify --output json: verify the attestation, convert the verified predicate into Pacto's own typed evidence, and evaluate Pacto's own requirements against it. That adapter lives in Pacto's repository, never in Aval. Aval will not grow Pacto-specific fields; any metadata Pacto (or any other tool) needs to carry goes in annotations, using reverse-DNS keys (for example dev.pacto.service). Aval never interprets annotations.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
Status: pre-alpha. Milestone 1 (contract + fingerprint) is implemented. Signing (attest.Sign), push, lookup and fetch (internal/registry), verification (evidence.Verify, attest.Verifier) and the policy file (policy.Load) are implemented; aval verify, aval run and aval push use them. This document describes the model the code is built around; where behavior is not implemented yet, it says so.

The predicate type, media types and the aval.trianalab.io/v1 apiVersion are frozen; see artifact-format.md.

docs.title: What a signature proves
docs.text:
An Aval attestation is a DSSE envelope around an in-toto Statement whose predicate (evidence.Predicate) says: "test test.id, with inputs hashing to execution.fingerprint, produced result on subject".

A valid signature proves:

  • Who claims it. The signer identity (OIDC issuer + certificate subject for keyless, or a key) is bound to the claim.
  • Integrity of the claim. The predicate has not been modified since it was signed.

A valid signature does not prove:

  • that the test actually ran;
  • that it ran honestly (unmodified test code, no skipped cases, no patched runner);
  • that inputs not declared in aval.yaml were the same. The fingerprint only covers what the contract declares (see contract.md). Anything else is invisible to Aval.

So reuse is never "the signature is valid". It is "the signature is valid, the signer is someone the policy trusts at a sufficient level, and the fingerprint and test id match what we computed locally".

runner.identity, runner.issuer and runner.trustLevel inside the predicate are what the signer claims. The authoritative identity is the verified signer, and the trust level is the one the policy grants to that signer, not the one written in the predicate. In code: attest.Verifier verifies the Sigstore bundle and returns the evidence.Signer it binds (the OIDC issuer and subject of the Fulcio certificate, or the key's id), and evidence.Verify looks that signer up in the policy's Identities with evidence.MatchSigner. A key-based signer only matches identities that list its public key; a keyless one only matches issuer and subject entries.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text:
attest.Sign (sigstore-go) signs the in-toto statement as a DSSE envelope in one of two modes:

  • Keyless (CI): an ephemeral key, a short-lived Fulcio certificate for the OIDC token the caller passes in, and a Rekor entry (always recorded, since the certificate expires in minutes and Rekor's timestamp is what makes it verifiable later). Signing always uses the Sigstore public-good instance (https://fulcio.sigstore.dev, https://rekor.sigstore.dev); the endpoints cannot be configured (TODO(milestone-5): signing against a private Sigstore deployment; verification already accepts its pinned trustedRoot). Obtaining the OIDC token is the caller's job, so no CI vendor or issuer is assumed.
  • Key-based (local): an unencrypted ECDSA P-256 PEM key (PKCS#8 or SEC1), for example from openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out aval.key. Cosign keys are encrypted and not supported. No Rekor entry. The bundle's key hint is the key's evidence.PublicKeyID. Expect policies to grant such signatures at most level 1.

Besides the envelope, Sign returns the Sigstore bundle (v0.3 JSON) with the verification material (certificate or key hint, Rekor entry). registry.Push requires it and stores it next to the envelope as the second layer of the execution manifest (see artifact-format.md).

docs.title: Trust levels
docs.text:
evidence.TrustLevel, higher is stronger:

Level Name Constant Who Good for 0 unknown TrustUnknown level could not be established never accepted 1 developer TrustDeveloper a developer's local signature personal acceleration only: skip a test you already ran on your machine. Not full trust. 2 runner TrustRunner a CI runner with a verifiable workload identity (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC) reuse in CI. CI should require at least this level. 3 isolated TrustIsolated an isolated execution with a verifiable attestation of the environment itself reuse where the runner host is not trusted either

Level 1 exists because a local signature is still useful to its author. Expect many security policies to refuse it outright; that is the intended use of MinTrustLevel.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
The trust policy decides which signers are accepted and at what level. It is policy.Policy (internal/policy), converted to evidence.VerifyOptions for evidence.Verify:

Field Meaning Identities accepted signers. Each evidence.Identity is either an OIDC Issuer plus a SubjectRegexp matched against the whole certificate subject (SAN), or a PublicKey, and the TrustLevel that signer is granted. Empty means nothing is accepted. MinTrustLevel minimum granted level required for reuse. Level 0 (unknown) and levels above 3 are never accepted, whatever this says. AllowedCacheability cacheability classes that may be reused besides hermetic and controlled-environment. Only external-dependencies has an effect; non-deterministic is never reusable. TrustedRoot Sigstore trusted root for keyless signatures (policy file only). ExpectedFingerprint, ExpectedTestID set by Aval from the local contract, not by the policy file.
